newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end near limit down.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end near limit down.

text.p: CME lumber futures tumbled sharply for the second day, finishing near limit down at 10-week lows on fund selling and pressure from weak cash, traders said.
Futures ended $9.80 to $3.00 per thousand board feet lower paced by July at $363.70 per tbf, the lowest price for July lumber since March 26. September ended $4.20 lower at $358.80.

Persistent new fund selling added to pressure and offset earlier short covering support, sending prices down to new lows for the move late. Back months had shown net gains earlier on short covering before also falling, traders said.
The bulk of the pressure continued to stem from lower-trending cash spruce prices. Demand for wood remains less than expected while production is high, they said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $362 per tbf, off $2 from last Friday. Cash lumber prices have fallen sharply from the recent high of $414 on February 21, tumbling to the lowest level since July 19, 1996, a Random Lengths source added.
Cargill Investor Services remain the most active seller in July, pit sources said.
Oriented Strand Board ended $3.90 to $4.60 per 1,000 sq. feet lower with July off $4.50 at $144.00 per 1,000 sq ft.
OSB hit resistance after closing up the daily limit Tuesday.
Values had surged Tuesday on reports of a fire destroying a Canadian OSB mill and the market was overbought, traders said.
